decision_note: Natural-history report documents nectar robbing by a wedge-billed hummingbird on a sicklebill-adapted Andean bellflower; legitimate pollination is system context, not a focal pollinator response measured against the same floral coordinate.

The masting study models synchronized intermittent reproduction under pollen limitation and specialist seed predation, but the focal state is reproductive timing/seed production rather than a declared floral attraction or display coordinate evaluated by both audiences.

The eutrophication dissertation analyzes bottom-up changes in flower-visitor, herbivore and parasitoid networks through plant-community composition; it does not evaluate one declared floral attraction/display coordinate A.

A_trait: herbivory- and water-stress-associated floral volatile blend
claim_ceiling: Induced-state mechanism only: floral volatile changes alter bumblebee attraction, but the antagonist is the antecedent herbivore treatment rather than a receiver responding to the same A and no common plant fitness outcome is measured.
decision_note: Full-text source shows combined water stress and whitefly herbivory alter Matthiola floral volatiles and bumblebee preference. Retained as a near-pass mechanism bridge, not a shared-A conflict test.

The blueberry thesis evaluates carpenter-bee nectar robbery and fruit quality, but the focal contrast is robber damage/behavior rather than an independently declared floral attraction/display coordinate A.

claim_ceiling: Antagonist/cheater use of flower-size geometry is identified, but the same-A legitimate pollinator response and plant reproductive outcome are absent.
decision_note: Fuchsia magellanica study links floral dimensions to bumblebee nectar-robbing behavior; retained as a one-channel shared-access near-pass.

claim_ceiling: Ficus phenological architecture is evaluated in a dual-role pollinating seed-predator system, but no manipulated A or paired receiver-response surface is identified; the proposed seasonality adaptation is rejected for F. aurea.
decision_note: Primary source tests costs and benefits of within-tree phenological synchrony in Ficus aurea, whose agaonid adults pollinate and larvae consume seeds. Retained as temporal-architecture near-pass only.
Duplicate bibliographic representation of the same 1992 Ficus aurea article retained as SCHPRISMA-000122; exclude from independent study counting.

Silene stellata mating-system study compares nursery-pollinating seed predators and generalist pollination in reproductive-system terms, but does not evaluate a declared floral attraction/display coordinate A.
Chemical communication article is a broad synthesis/commentary rather than an independent primary shared-cue study; retain for citation chasing only.

A_trait: species-specific floral scent blend / component ratio
claim_ceiling: Resolved pollinator odor specificity tests the private-channel hypothesis in a pollinating seed-predator mutualism, but larval seed predation is not measured as a receiver response to the same odor code and no common plant fitness surface is present.
decision_note: Breynia–Epicephala study resolves species-specific pollinator scent responses and explicitly tests a private-channel hypothesis. Retained as a same-code architecture near-pass, not evidence of historical privatization.
Silene circadian study measures petal/nectar/scent rhythms, floral visitation and pollination success, but no focal plant antagonist response to the floral timing coordinate is measured.

Kadsura study reconstructs coevolution of resin-filled floral nurseries with pollinating resin midges, but larvae feed on resin rather than pollen, ovules or seeds; it does not supply a focal antagonist/exploiter response to a floral attraction coordinate for SCH.

A_trait: female-flower morphology and specialized pollinating-seed-predator association
claim_ceiling: Direct evidence for dynamic codiversification, host shifts and changing interaction modularity in a pollinating seed-predator mutualism; no floral cue state is reconstructed, so this does not establish shared-to-private cue evolution.
decision_note: Dissertation documents Epicephala active pollination, larval seed consumption, repeated island colonizations, host shifts and changing network modularity. Retained only in the evolutionary-outcome lane.

Chamaecrista dissertation links morphology, pollination, herbivory and ant defense, but direct causal tests center on extrafloral resources and do not evaluate one declared floral A against both receiver classes.

Mimulus flower-longevity study measures coflowering context, pollinator visitation/pollen transfer and female fitness, but the coflowering community is not a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response to the same floral A.
Colourful cones article is a synthesis/perspective on the evolution of flower colour rather than an independent primary shared-cue study.

Comparative Sileneae scent phylogeny analyzes day/night floral emissions and pollinator-guild interpretation; antagonist roles are contextual and not measured as a focal response to the same scent coordinate.

Land-use gradient study crosses aphid infestation, natural enemies and pollination services, but the causal/spatial contrast is habitat and aphid pressure rather than a declared floral attraction/display coordinate A.
Ant–plant study manipulates or compares extrafloral nectar/honeydew resource pathways affecting defense, pollination and fitness; the focal resource axis is not a floral attraction/display signal.

JA/SA induction study connects defense signaling to floral chemistry, pollination and seed-predator damage, but the manipulated coordinate is systemic defense state rather than a declared floral attraction/display A. Retain as cross-project provenance, not SCH one-trait evidence.

A_trait: population-differentiated floral morphology in Lithophragma bolanderi
claim_ceiling: Geographic local adaptation and divergence in pollination efficacy are supported in a dual-role pollinating seed-parasite system; floral traits are not randomized, so this is near-pass/evolutionary evidence rather than a strict shared-A experiment.
decision_note: Ecology 2023 study shows two Sierra Nevada populations differ in floral morphology and pollinator communities; local moths pollinate local plants more efficiently and G. politella oviposition behavior differs among populations.

Impatiens experiment manipulates florivory, nectar robbing and pollination supplementation and measures reproduction, but the manipulated factors are consumer interactions rather than a declared floral attraction/display A.
Secondary nectar-robbing study estimates consequences for male reproductive success; the focal contrast is robber behavior/damage rather than an independently declared floral A.
Study addresses constraints on signals/rewards to multiple mutualists (pollinators and seed dispersers), not a focal plant antagonist/exploiter channel.
AMF experiment changes belowground symbiosis and measures herbivory/pollinator behavior, while floral traits are not the manipulated coordinate and were not the identified mediator.

A_trait: scape length, flower number and petal size in Primula farinosa
claim_ceiling: Opposing pollinator versus seed-predator/grazer selection on floral display and spatially varying net selection support compromise and geographic evolutionary mosaics; no randomized do(A) or historical cue privatization.
decision_note: Primula farinosa thesis/manuscript reports pollinators selecting for conspicuous display while seed predators/grazers oppose it, with net selection varying among populations. Treat as the same biological research program as SCHPRISMA-000523 for independence-sensitive synthesis.
Datura defense-induction experiment changes reproductive traits and seed output, but pollinator attractiveness is inferred rather than measured as a focal pollinator response in the study.

Leaf-damage dissertation measures subsequent floral visitors and odor changes after mechanical damage, but herbivory/damage is the antecedent treatment rather than a declared floral A evaluated by both audiences.

Flower-defense dissertation integrates florivores, induced defense, volatiles, pollinators and fitness, but its causal contrasts are herbivore/pathogen/defense states rather than one declared floral attraction/display coordinate A.

The Würzburg dissertation on defensive floral scents is highly relevant by title, but a source-verifiable full text could not be recovered in the registered open-source audit. Preserve as retrieval failure rather than biological exclusion.

claim_ceiling: Floral stickiness causally reduces florivory and increases fruit set, with population-specific effects; pollinator response to the same stickiness manipulation is not directly measured, so the study is near-pass rather than strict.
decision_note: Scientific Reports 2022 directly manipulates petal stickiness, measures florivory and fruit set, and reports population-specific effects. Hummingbird exclusion does not provide a direct pollinator response to do(stickiness).

Tree reproductive-density study evaluates conspecific density and reproductive success; high floral/seed density is ecological context, not a declared floral attraction/display coordinate with paired receiver responses.

claim_ceiling: Direct synthetic same-code assay shows bumblebee attraction and ant repulsion, supporting receiver separability/opposite response; ant role is conditional and no plant reproductive outcome is measured, so this is not strict and does not prove privacy.
decision_note: Plant Signaling & Behavior addendum reports empirical bumblebee and ant responses to synthetic floral scent compounds, extending the associated meta-analysis with a direct same-code behavioral contrast.
Determining factors of flower coloration is a review/synthesis article rather than an independent primary shared-cue study.
